summary: M.S. Computer Engineering candidate at Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) graduating May 2026, focused on perception and embedded robotics. Built ROS2 and YOLO-based perception pipelines integrating cameras, ToF range sensors, and inertial sensors for real-time obstacle detection and visual servoing on Jetson and STM32 platforms. Experienced validating perception software through simulation (CARLA), recorded-data testing, and physical field trials in C++ and Python on Linux.

experience.title: Research Intern (Capstone)
bullets: Deployed ZoeDepth monocular depth estimation for crack-depth profiling, achieving ±8% error on 3D surface reconstruction.
Architected a full perception pipeline for microscopic crack analysis combining image processing, denoising, and depth estimation.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition system integrating ADXL345 inertial sensors with Raspberry Pi over I2C and HC-05 Bluetooth.
Implemented a custom sensor-processing algorithm using z-axis thresholding; resolved sensor jitter via software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: Deep Learning Intern
bullets: Curated and labeled a custom object-detection dataset of 1,133 images for health-level classification using YOLOv8.
Trained YOLOv8n achieving 83% mAP@50 on held-out validation; exported to ONNX and TFLite for embedded/mobile deployment.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a vision-guided perception pipeline with TensorRT-optimized YOLO (5.2x speedup, 17.6->92 FPS) fused with dual VL53L0X ToF sensors via I2C for contact-aware obstacle/grasp detection.
Achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end latency on a Jetson+Arduino embedded stack; resolved 11 field-integration failures (false positives, stale frames, sensor timing).

projects.name: Autonomous Driving Perception in CARLA
bullets: Built CARLA simulation pipelines using semantic segmentation and raycast occlusion filtering to auto-generate ~5,000 YOLO and ~3,000 lane-detection training frames.
Trained YOLO11n (mAP50 ~0.85) and fine-tuned a ResNet-18 lane-detection model; integrated into a perception-to-control stack with waypoint fallback.
Validated in simulation with 30 vehicles and 10 pedestrians, achieving zero collisions and correct traffic-light compliance across multiple laps.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Built a real-time perception-to-actuation pipeline using YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect/track objects, sending control commands to an STM32 over UART.
Integrated VL53L0X ToF range sensing alongside camera detection for redundant obstacle awareness, with FreeRTOS-based multi-servo PWM control.

projects.name: ROS-Based Robotic Arm (AL5B & UR5e)
bullets: Derived DH tables and forward kinematic chains for a 6-DoF UR5e and 5-DoF AL5B; validated against MoveIt/RViz URDF models in ROS 2 Humble and ROS Noetic.
Planned collision-free pick-and-place trajectories on a physical UR5e via the UR ROS 2 driver; measured AL5B repeatability at <2mm over 10 trials.

awards: 1st Prize, Poster Presentation — 2D and 3D Image Mosaicing of Microscopic Images, F.C.R.I.T. (2024)
1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
